chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) looked at a man who was saying, 'O Allah, I ask You from Your permissible sustenance.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'You are asking for the subsistence of the Prophets. Say, O Allah, I ask You for a permissible, extensive, goodly sustenance from Your sustenance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for abundant and high-quality sustenance in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) refines the concept of *rizq* by distinguishing between mere permissibility (*halal*) and the elevated quality of sustenance enjoyed by the Prophets. He instructs the supplicant to seek *was'a* (abundance/wideness) and *tayyib* (purity/delicacy), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on seeking not just the absence of prohibition, but the presence of divine grace and ease in one's livelihood. This guidance underscores the spiritual dimension of material needs, encouraging believers to aspire to a sustenance that facilitates worship and well-being.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> looked towards a man and he was saying, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Permissible sustenance’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You are asking for the subsistence of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>. Say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for Permissible sustenance, extensive, goodly, from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Sustenance’’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) saying, ‘

Once abu Ja’far (a.s.) looked upon a man who was saying, “O Lord, I plead before You for lawful sustenance.” Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to him, ‘You are asking the sustenance of the prophets, say, “O Lord, I plead before You for lawful sustenance from You that is vast and pure.’”
